action: Customers of JPMorgan, Mastercard and Visa programs: expect phishing that uses your name or email, and do not act on unsolicited messages.
date_note: Date of the companies' statements: ABC13 (read 2026-11-19) says JPMorganChase made its statement Thursday morning (19 November); the date of the attack itself is not stated.
exec: Vendor incidents reached marketing data held for major banking and card brands; customers face phishing risk.
plain: Visa, JPMorgan and Mastercard say outside vendors were hacked. JPMorgan and Mastercard say some customer email addresses may be exposed. Visa and Mastercard say their own systems or payment network were not affected.
summary: JPMorganChase said attackers accessed marketing data held by its vendors that may include some customer names and email addresses; it will offer free credit monitoring where appropriate. Visa tied the claims to an Asia Pacific provider and said its systems and card numbers were not affected. Mastercard cited a limited amount of cardholder emails. SecurityWeek, relaying Reuters, says N0n claimed the data; Reuters' review found over 16,000 customer emails.
title: Visa, JPMorgan and Mastercard say third-party providers were hit; n0n gang claims it, per SOCRadar
